nodes.name: Oxidative ligand exchange
nodes.procedure: MnO2 electrodeposited on a corrosion-resistant platinum-coated titanium mesh (MnO2/PTL) (33) was immersed in 0.01 M H2SO4 containing K2IrCl6 at 95°C for 6 hours to yield the precatalyst (Ir-pre). Almost all Ir atoms (>99%) were captured by MnO2 from the K2IrCl6 precursor solution after 6 hours of reaction.

nodes.description: OER mass activity comparison in three-electrode system
nodes.source_text: In a three-electrode system containing 1M H2SO4 (pH 0) as the electrolyte, IrVI-ado showed a 10-fold higher mass activity compared with that of benchmark rutile IrO2 (Elyst Ir75) at an iridium loading of 0.02 mgIr cm−2 at 1.6 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) (figs. S23 to S26). The same trend was also confirmed when the activity was evaluated using the electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) (fig. S26)

nodes.description: Long-term PEM electrolysis stability at 1 A/cm² with different loadings
nodes.source_text: Cell voltages were measured at mass-specific activities of 5×10^4, 2.5×10^4, and 1.25×10^4 A gIr^−1 (1 A cm^−2 using 0.02, 0.04, and 0.08 mgIr cm^−2, respectively). Under each condition, the average degradation rates were 84.3, 12.4, and −10.7 μV hour^−1, respectively.

nodes.description: In situ XAS analysis during PEM electrolysis at varying cell voltages
nodes.source_text: A MEA sample of IrVI-ado with 0.08 mgIr cm^−2 was used for in situ XAS analysis under industrial water electrolysis conditions (≥1.0 A cm^−2 and 80°C). X-ray absorption spectra were collected at cell voltages of 1.5, 1.8, and 2.5 V... where the current densities reached 0.02, 0.42, and 2.30 A cm^−2, respectively. The change in Ir L3 WL position upon increasing the cell voltage was <0.1 eV

nodes.description: Optimized PEM electrolysis performance with p-PTL substrate
nodes.source_text: Using this optimized setup, the current density reached 4.0 A cm^−2 at a cell voltage of 2.0 V (Fig. 4F)... The mass activity exceeded 1.7×10^5 A gIr^−1 at 1.75 V after iR (i, current; R, resistance) correction... Long-term electrolysis for 2700 hours at 2.25×10^4 A gIr^−1 was demonstrated at a cell voltage of ~1.8 V [energy efficiency of 82% versus higher heating value (HHV)]
the Faradaic efficiency at 2.2 A cm^−2 was determined to be 100±3% (fig. S30,A to C)

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Ir L3-edge XAS during synthesis shows white line shift indicating Ir oxidation from +4 to higher state; EXAFS reveals Ir-Cl (2.33 Å) → Ir-O (1.96 Å) ligand exchange and new Ir-O-Mn peak at 2.92 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The white line (WL) peak of the iridium L3 edge in the x-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra shifted to higher energy by 0.9 eV during the reaction at 95°C in H2SO4 and a further 0.5 eV during the subsequent calcination at 450°C, which indicates that iridium was oxidized from 4 to a higher oxidation state (Fig. 1, B to D).

nodes.characterization_summary: HERFD-XANES at Ir L3-edge estimates IrVI-ado oxidation state as +5.8±0.1, consistent with d³ electron configuration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Using this approach, IrVI-ado was estimated to have oxidation states of +5.8±0.1 (Fig. 2B and figs. S5 to S7). This is consistent with the oxidation state predicted from the L3 + L2 WL intensities (+5.75; fig. S6) and confirms the formation of hexavalent IrVI with an electron configuration of d³.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir 4f XPS shows symmetric peaks at 62.61 eV (Ir 4f7/2) and 65.61 eV (Ir 4f5/2), confirming hexavalent IrVI as dominant species (>80%).
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution x-ray photoemission spectroscopy (XPS) was also used to confirm the formation of hexavalent IrVI by determining its intrinsic binding energy. The Ir 4f peaks of IrVI-ado showed symmetric Gaussian-Lorentzian (SGL) line shapes for both Ir 4f7/2 and Ir 4f5/2 (Fig. 2C), which were located at binding energies of 62.61 eV and 65.61 eV, respectively.

properties.description: Proton Exchange Membrane with 0.08 mg/cm² loading

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows IrVI-ado covers PTL substrate uniformly.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) showed that the obtained IrVI-ado covered the PTL substrate uniformly (Fig. 2D).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images show iridium atoms atomically dispersed (bright dots) embedded in MnO2 surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Atomic-resolution high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) images showed that iridium was atomically dispersed on the MnO2 oxide support (Fig. 2, E to G).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Ir L3-edge XAS during PEM electrolysis at current densities up to 2.30 A cm^{-2} shows <0.1 eV white line shift, confirming maintenance of hexavalent IrVI state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Using in situ electrochemical XAS measurements, we confirmed that the IrVI-ado maintained a high valence (IrVI) under OER conditions in a PEM electrolyzer (Fig. 3, A and B).

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS shows complete Ir-Cl to Ir-O ligand exchange (1.96 Å, shorter than rutile IrO2) and Ir-O-Mn coordination at 2.92 Å indicating Ir substitution into MnO2 lattice.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Calcination at 450°C resulted in the complete replacement of chloride by oxygen, yielding an average Ir-O bond length of 1.96 Å for IrVI-ado (fig. S14). ... A new peak assigned to Ir-O-Mn coordination appeared at 2.92 Å during the iridium oxidation by MnO2 in H2SO4 and became more pronounced during calcination (Fig. 1G and figs. S13 to S15).
